title: Word Search II
summary: Provide all words found on an m x n character board, using adjacent cells for word construction without reusing letters within a word.
statement: Provide all words found on an m x n character board, using adjacent cells for word construction without reusing letters within a word.
constraints: The board has 1–12 rows and columns of lowercase English letters. words contains 1–30000 UNIQUE lowercase strings, each 1–10 letters long.
A word follows horizontal/vertical neighbors; a cell cannot be reused within that word. Different words may reuse cells. Return each found dictionary word once, in any order.
target_time_complexity: O(S + rows×columns×4×3^(L-1)) worst case, S is total dictionary length and L≤10
hints: Many dictionary words share prefixes, so their searches can share work too.
Store words in a trie and explore board paths only while they match a trie prefix.
Mark a cell during recursive exploration, follow matching orthogonal neighbors, restore the cell on return, and remove an emitted word marker to avoid duplicates.
Keep longer continuations after finding a prefix word. Delete a trie branch only when it contains no remaining word or child.
editorial: The trie shares prefix exploration across the dictionary. A board-frequency precheck removes impossible words before insertion. Recursive DFS marks only the current path, restores every cell, and emits each terminal word once. Empty trie branches can be removed after exploration because they contain no unfound words. Recursion depth is bounded by the maximum word length, ten, even on a 12×12 board. The independent oracle performs per-word breadth-by-character state expansion using explicit used-cell bitmasks, with no trie or board mutation. This returns a set of dictionary matches rather than the existing single-word Boolean.

tests.explanation: The board contains oath and eat along orthogonal paths; pea and rain have no valid paths. Either output order is accepted.
A matching route cannot reuse a cell, and the required second b cannot be reached legally; no word is returned.
